stories.headline: Burnham’s soft launch is ending as hard foreign policy issues loom
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Burnham's soft launch is ending as hard foreign policy issues loom. The prime minister faces challenges such as backing Ukraine against Russian threats and redefining relations with the US. Burnham has accepted the constraints of Boris Johnson's hard Brexit and Britain's security dependency on Washington, limiting his room for innovation in foreign policy. Former Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrei Fedorov warned that the UK could face a "semi-military" response from unknown sources for sharing military blueprints with Ukraine. Burnham will need to build relations on the international stage, with issues such as climate change and defence budgets also requiring attention. The prime minister's response to these challenges will be crucial, with Labour having a rare opportunity to play an international leadership role in addressing global security challenges. Burnham's approach to foreign policy will be closely watched in the coming days.

stories.headline: New UK prime minister would rather focus on domestic policy over foreign, but that’s what they all say until geopolitics intrudes
stories.summary: Andy Burnham has become the new UK prime minister, replacing Sir Keir Starmer. Burnham, the fourth prime minister in five years, aims to focus on domestic policy, particularly tackling the cost-of-living crisis. He has appointed Ed Miliband as Foreign Secretary, a role that may gain importance if the prime minister's attention is on domestic matters. This approach is not unprecedented, as former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak also prioritized domestic policy and gave his Foreign Secretary, David Cameron, independence to lead on foreign policy. Despite the intention to focus on domestic issues, the UK's geopolitical landscape may still require the prime minister's attention, as has been the case with previous leaders. Burnham's leadership of the Labour Party began on Friday, and he will now lead the country from No 10 Downing Street.

stories.headline: LANDBANK, OFBank open 211K ID-free accounts in one month
stories.summary: State-run Landbank and Overseas Filipino Bank (OFBank) have opened over 211,000 National ID-enabled accounts without physical IDs within a month of launch. The accounts were opened through a system that authenticates identities using the National ID system, eliminating the need for customers to present or upload a physical government-issued ID. This development reflects strong demand for more accessible financial services. The National ID-enabled service was rolled out in July, and the significant number of accounts opened in the first month indicates a high level of interest in convenient and digital banking services. The initiative aims to increase access to financial services, particularly for those who may not have traditional forms of identification. The successful rollout is expected to promote financial inclusion and expand the reach of banking services in the country.

stories.headline: Should You Buy Marvell Technology Stock Before Aug. 27?
stories.summary: Marvell Technology is set to release its fiscal second-quarter financial results on August 27. The company's stock has risen over 160% year to date, but has retreated from its highest point this week. Options traders are preparing for significant volatility, with a potential 14% stock price swing in either direction, equivalent to a $30 per share movement. Marvell Technology has a history of beating earnings expectations and has already raised its guidance. The company has also formed a deal with Google, extending a previous partnership. Ahead of the earnings report, Marvell Technology stock has pulled back from its year-to-date high of $330, forming an inverted head-and-shoulders pattern. Investors are waiting to see if the stock will continue its upward trend or experience a correction after the earnings announcement. The report will be closely watched by market participants.

stories.headline: 5% Dividend Stock Worth Considering for Monthly Income
stories.summary: CT REIT offers a 5.37% yield, with a monthly payout of $0.0818 per unit, or $0.98 per unit annually. Another option, Choice, provides a 5% annualized dividend yield with monthly distributions of $0.065 per unit, equivalent to $0.78 per unit yearly. Main Street Capital, a popular choice for monthly-income portfolios, yields 5.73% with a regular monthly dividend of $0.265 and a quarterly supplemental dividend of $0.30. Realty Income and Clearway also offer attractive dividend yields, with Realty Income's monthly dividend yielding 5% and Clearway raising its payment every quarter since late 2020. These stocks may be worth considering for investors seeking monthly income, but it's essential to evaluate their dividend safety by reviewing recurring earnings, NAV trends, leverage, and distribution history before making an investment decision.

stories.headline: Businesses Are Shunning Anthropic’s Fable 5 for Cheaper Models
stories.summary: Anthropic's Fable 5 model is facing low demand from businesses due to its high price. As a result, the model is being surpassed by cheaper alternatives, including Anthropic's own Opus 5, which has seen higher business spending since its launch in late July. Fable 5 is designed for complex tasks such as coding and research, but analysts say older models can handle most business needs. The high price of Fable 5 is a major factor in its low demand, raising questions about the sustainability of developing ultra-premium models. If Fable 5's revenue share remains in the single digits, it may become difficult for Anthropic to justify the high development costs. This trend is part of a larger shift in AI spending, with businesses becoming more cautious about investing in advanced models. Anthropic's ability to sustain Fable 5's development is now under scrutiny.
